name: Timothy, with Lois and Eunice
charge: Unfeigned faith that dwelt first in his grandmother and his mother; knowing the holy scriptures from a child
summary: Paul came to Derbe and Lystra and found a disciple named Timotheus, son of a believing Jewess, whose father was a Greek; the brethren there spoke well of him, and Paul circumcised him and took him along (Acts 16:1-3). Paul called to remembrance the unfeigned faith that dwelt first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice, and was persuaded it was in Timothy also (2 Timothy 1:5), and reminded him that from a child he had known the holy scriptures, which are able to make a man wise to salvation (2 Timothy 3:14-15).
offenseFull: Greek in this account does not mean another nation. His father was a hellenized Jew, a man of the northern kingdom living in the Greek customs, which is why the boy had never been circumcised; his mother and grandmother were Israelite women raised under the law of Moses, and they raised him in it (Acts 16:1). Paul circumcised him because of the Jews in those quarters and took him on the journey (Acts 16:2-3). The teaching of children in the law at home is the commandment itself, to be taught diligently to the children and talked of in the house and by the way (Deuteronomy 6:6-7), with the promise that a child trained in the way he should go does not depart from it when he is old (Proverbs 22:6). Two women in one household kept a boy in the scriptures while the man of the house did not, and by the time the apostle arrived the work was already done.

Paul called to remembrance the unfeigned faith that dwelt first in Lois and then in Eunice, and said he was persuaded it was in Timothy too (2 Timothy 1:5). Unfeigned means not put on, not a false appearance; the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart and of a good conscience and of faith unfeigned (1 Timothy 1:5). That family was sincere through three generations, and Paul saw it. He told the young man that from a child he had known the holy scriptures, which are able to make a man wise to salvation through faith in Christ, and that all scripture given by inspiration is profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:14-17). He told him to stir up the gift of God that was in him by the putting on of his hands (2 Timothy 1:6), which is what Moses did to Joshua, so that Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom and the children of Israel hearkened to him (Deuteronomy 34:9). Paul knew he was about to be beheaded in Rome. The letters were written to get the young man ready to stand where he had stood.
judgmentFull: Paul called him his own son in the faith (1 Timothy 1:2), committed the charge to him that he might war a good warfare (1 Timothy 1:18), and told him to let no man despise his youth but to be an example of the believers in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity (1 Timothy 4:12). The teaching applies that to every young man the Lord sets over a congregation: you may be young, but you are not a novice, and the first thing the men creeping in will try is to hem you up on your age. Show the example because the hearts of the brethren depend on it (Judith 8:24). Paul told him to give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine, and not to neglect the gift in him, given by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery (1 Timothy 4:13-14), and warned him that all who will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution, as Paul himself had at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra (2 Timothy 3:11-12). And of all the men around him Paul said he had none likeminded who would naturally care for the state of the congregation; the proof of this one was that, as a son with the father, he had served with him in the gospel (Philippians 2:19-22). Paul greatly desired to see him, being mindful of his tears, that he might be filled with joy (2 Timothy 1:3-4). That is what a family that kept a child in the scriptures produced.

taught.title: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children
Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

text.text: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also.
Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:
But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them;
And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.
All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.
And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.
Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare;
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.
Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.
Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.
Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me.
Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.
But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.
For I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state.
For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ’s.
But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.
I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of thee in my prayers night and day;
Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy;
